messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

1. Net worth of Lionel Messi in Euros.
2. Net worth of LeBron James in British Pounds.
3. BMI of a person weighing 85 kg and height 180 cm using metric system.
4. BMI of a person weighing 200 pounds and height 6 ft 2 in using imperial system.

We have two functions: calculate_bmi and celebrity_net_worth_get.

We need to call celebrity_net_worth_get twice with appropriate parameters. For Messi: name "Lionel Messi", currency "EUR". For LeBron: name "LeBron James", currency "GBP".

Then we need to call calculate_bmi twice. For first: weight 85, height 180, unit default metric. For second: weight 200, height 6 ft 2 in. But calculate_bmi expects weight in kilograms and height in centimeters. It also has optional unit param. But it doesn't accept weight in pounds or height in feet/inches directly. We might need to convert manually. But the function signature says weight: number, height: number, unit?: string. So if we pass unit 'imperial', maybe the function handles conversion internally. But the description says "Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax." It doesn't specify how it interprets unit. Likely if unit is 'imperial', weight should be in pounds and height in inches. So we can pass weight=200, height=74 (6*12+2), unit='imperial'.

Thus calls:

celebrity_net_worth_get({"name":"Lionel Messi","currency":"EUR"})
celebrity_net_worth_get({"name":"LeBron James","currency":"GBP"})
calculate_bmi({"weight":85,"height":180})
calculate_bmi({"weight":200,"height":74,"unit":"imperial"})

We need to output results. We'll call functions sequentially.
